tasks.short: Monitor woodworking machines and correct deviations

steps.what: Monitor machine operation and compare workpiece condition with specifications
Make appropriate machine adjustments and check the resulting workpiece

tasks.design: Retain observation, diagnosis of deviations and physical adjustments. Specifications in {DOCS} remain references; no general model is placed in the machine control path.
tasks.previous_blocker: Wood variability and tool condition change the result during operation.
tasks.enabler_now: Administrative technology does not establish equivalent physical monitoring or correction.
tasks.still_hard: A surface defect may have several mechanical or material causes.
tasks.human_edge: The operator recognises unsafe or abnormal behaviour and tests corrections on the actual workpiece.
tasks.altitude: Operating responsibility and time remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Fault escalation and safe intervention boundaries

evidence.claim: Retaining physical monitoring and adjustment is an E1 assessment from model knowledge; no research digest was supplied.

assumptions: Boundary is monitoring and correction during production, excluding machine runtime and initial setup.
No new sensor coverage, structured defect code or automated adjustment is presumed.
Existing specifications and controls remain; no custom system is proposed.
Zero upkeep because no workflow changes.
unknowns: Machine types and routine adjustment duties
research_questions: Which observed deviations require operator adjustment and which require maintenance?

tasks.short: Determine woodworking specifications and setup requirements

steps.what: Interpret blueprints and instructions to determine materials, methods and setup requirements

tasks.design: Retain interpretation of drawings and instructions in {DOCS}, with clarification of conflicts before setup. No extractor is treated as authoritative for dimensions, material or work method.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instructions may omit practical material or machine constraints.
tasks.enabler_now: Document access does not remove the operator's interpretation work.
tasks.still_hard: Grain, finish, tolerances and machine capability interact.
tasks.human_edge: The operator recognises when a literal drawing instruction is incomplete or impractical.
tasks.altitude: Specification interpretation and method decisions remain unchanged.

reach.task: Identify an unclear work-order requirement before scheduling

evidence.claim: Keeping specification and method interpretation human is an E1 assessment from model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is determining requirements, not subsequent programming or physical setup.
No free structured dimensions or automatic method selection is assumed.
Existing document facilities remain; no custom build is proposed.
Zero upkeep because this work does not change.
research_questions: Which missing requirements most often require clarification before work begins?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 net0. Interpretation remains counted; no invented drawing-transcription baseline is removed.

steps.what: Select knives, blades, cutter heads, bits or belts for the required operation

tasks.design: Keep tooling selection and condition assessment with the operator. Tool guidance in {DOCS} supports the decision; a catalogue match alone does not establish suitability for the actual machine and wood.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tool choice depends on condition as well as nominal dimensions.
tasks.enabler_now: A searchable catalogue does not remove physical condition checks or compatibility judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Wear, material characteristics and finish requirements affect the choice.
tasks.human_edge: The operator recognises unsuitable or damaged tooling before use.
tasks.altitude: Tool-selection authority and time remain unchanged.

No structured safe-tool flag or machine selection action is assumed.
Existing instructions remain; no custom selection tool is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because no process changes.
research_questions: Which compatibility or condition issues cannot be resolved from the catalogue alone?

tasks.short: Program and set up woodworking CNC machines

steps.what: Select a proven repeat-part programme and determine its job-specific parameters
Program repeat-part parameter values into the selected CNC routine
Verify the programme, set up the machine and conduct a controlled trial
Inspect the trial workpiece and decide whether setup needs correction

tasks.design: For established repeat-part families, configure the existing CAD/CNC programming system {OTHER} to populate a proven parameterised routine from a checked sheet. Keep programme verification, physical setup, controlled trial and first-piece inspection with the operator; new geometry or unproven routines stay manual.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated parameter entry can be separate from choosing dimensions and safe machining strategy.
tasks.enabler_now: Native parameterised routines can reuse fixed proven logic without generating a new strategy.
tasks.still_hard: Tooling, workholding, coordinate systems and actual cutting behaviour require validation.
tasks.human_edge: The operator judges whether the routine applies and checks the physical result.
tasks.altitude: Less repeat-parameter typing, with setup and release decisions unchanged.

reach.task: Specify the boundary of a reusable repeat-part routine
reach.learn: Parameter validation, simulation and revision control

evidence.claim: Using native parameterised routines for proven repeat parts is an E1 model-knowledge design; no digest or measured woodworking case was supplied.

assumptions: Boundary is repeat-part programming and initial setup, excluding continuous monitoring and the separate requirements/tooling decisions. Novel work remains manually programmed.

The operator produces routine ID/version, machine ID, units, dimensions, origin, tooling IDs and applicable parameter values in s1, retaining all 25 hours for capture and checking. Missing or incompatible fields require manual programming.
An existing proven routine library is a customer prerequisite, not newly generated machine knowledge. Test native parameter import before custom code; if absent, do not adopt this saving scenario.

Allow five focal hours for routine upkeep and parameter exceptions beyond job checks. s3 includes simulation or equivalent native verification before loading and controlled trial; s4 follows the actual trial.
unknowns: Manual repeated-entry share and native verification facilities
research_questions: Can repeat parameters populate the exact approved routine without changing paths, workholding assumptions or first-piece quality?
